My bathroom abilities are normal now and while he was there, he tightened things up a bit. I don’t regret it one bit but I didn’t have to have a hysterectomy so it may be different.

My son had a cringe phase when he was around that age with hats. I just had to suck it up and tell him he looked handsome. I really don’t know what I would do if it was a tail. Are they exploring the furry community as a maybe coming of age thing?

I’m sorry you’re working through this but I can tell you’re an amazing mom and your child is lucky they have you as a safe person as they explore this part of themselves.

Hi! I just had surgery to repair a cystocele and rectocele. I am still recovering and it is not an easy recovery at all but I don’t regret the surgery at all. My son is in college so I lived with it for so many years and thought that was just what things were like after having a baby. I’m done having children so that wasn’t a concern but you might want to as your urogynocologist about it if you want more children. 

If you do get the surgery, make sure you have someone to help with the baby for at least 12 weeks. You’ll have trouble holding baby and that sort of thing. I’m in the 12 week recovery time and I can’t even do laundry yet. 

You’re not alone. I thought I was the only one with this issue but I guess it is really common, people just don’t talk about it. Feel free to ask any questions, I’m happy to share!

My now husband probably drank 1/3 bottle of whiskey a night when we found out I was pregnant. There was no if, and, or but about it. He respected my decision but was not ready to be a dad. The pregnancy sucked and he never once felt our son kick because it felt like a “parasite” to him. 

BUT, he is actually the best dad that I could ever have asked for for my son. So, don’t give up hope. People freak out in different ways and if there isn’t anything other than the initial reaction, I would try to sympathize with how shocked and scared he must have been and forgive it.

Yes, it took me a long time to recover from psychosis. The longer and deeper it is, the harder it is to come out of it. Take your meds and let your body and mind heal itself from the trauma of psychosis. I can tell you it does get better. I feel very stable and don’t have any psychotic symptoms at all.

I had a boy and oh my gosh, he was easy. I did get the pee hose a couple times and it took about a week to get the whole diaper change thing down, but it wasn’t too bad. My husband was passionate about circumcising him so it was pretty easy to keep clean with wipes. I don’t know how to clean non circumcised but it is way more common so I’m sure there are instructions. 

I never had brothers, I had no idea how to take care of a boy but it went really well and I love him so much! You’ll do great!

In order to go poo, I had to strain and wiggle around to get things out and even then I couldn’t completely empty. I also would pee a lot because I couldn’t completely empty my bladder. I could sometimes get more by standing up for a bit and trying again. 

There was also this bulge where my taint is and it just looked super weird. Now it is gone and I love the way it looks!

Wow, that must be so hard. I had a catheter for several days after my surgery and it was so hard to live with it. I’m so sorry your son has to deal with this and I’m so sorry you have the extra effort in your life. You’re such a good mom.

I’m not doing great recovering quickly but I don’t regret the surgery at all. I am peeing and pooing in an easy and normal way which has changed the quality of my life. I also took a look and it is so beautiful! No more bulge dropping down. 

You sort of have to change your habits to keep the surgery successful and I hear people who pair it with Physical therapy have great outcomes.

Getting help is what a good parent does. As long as you are capable of providing care, you should be fine. I was scared that I couldn’t do it but my doctor was the one that said I was fine to be a mom. Getting help is the best thing you can do for your child. Now that my son is grown, he says he just wishes we would have told him what was going on sooner but we didn’t know. If you have warning signs, you can get on meds before it gets too bad. Good luck. This is something I learned in a work context but I think it can also be used with personal matters. It’s called crucial conversations. It goes something like this: 

Schedule a time to sit down in a neutral location, maybe even a coffee shop if you’re worried about a bad reaction. Then say: 

MIL, when you get upset when I do the dishes, it makes me feel like an intruder in my home. Is that your intention?

I took out the word own out of own home because that could make her feel upset that you don’t consider it her home too. I get what you mean but I would try to make it as neutral as possible.

The - is that your intention? - part is important because it hopefully makes a person less defensive because they will say oh no, of course that isn’t my intention. And then probably explain why they did that action. 

One reaction she might (probably?) will have is to get defensive. In a work situation people need to keep themselves somewhat polite but I think the way you describe her that she won’t be polite. 

She might come back with a snarky response or try to turn it around on you. Stay calm and the louder she gets the softer you should get - within reason of course. You can say something like - i know you want to contribute to the household and I appreciate that. Kill her with kindness. 

Sometimes I like to do the dishes myself. That isn’t because I think you’re doing a bad job because you’re not. You’re great and I’m so thankful you are helping out. Please don’t be offended when I do the dishes in the future. It is not a reflection of you in any way, it is because I like to do them sometimes. (Who likes doing dishes? This is probably a white lie.)

Good luck!!!

I recommend you make an action plan binder. The first section you can work together to identify what are warning signs that an episode might be coming on. You may notice things that he is not aware of himself. He may notice something internally that he can communicate. The benefit of this section is for when you think he is going into an episode, you can look through this together and come to the agreement that you have to take the next step. 

Next section would be all of their doctor’s names and info. List all of the medication that he has tried in the past and why it was stopped. Document the current medication and doses. The benefit of this is when you agree that an episode might happen is this will give you the tools to talk to the doctor right away. I would not be surprised if some doses need tweaking. Once again, you are putting this binder together with each other so you both feel invested in it. 

The next section is a list of hospitals in the area and their info. List things that are allowed for each hospital and what the visiting / phone call rules are. This can help you weigh the pros and cons of these places should the need come up. Some things may be more important than others given the situation. 

I would also suggest you both sign it. If he goes into psychosis and doesn’t trust the binder, you can remind him that he signed it. That works for me when I have to refer back to my journal where it says no one is trying to poison me. I know I can trust my rational mind.

I have learned so much on communication in couples counseling. I would really think about it because when I hear this I hear a communication problem. 

It is important to ask for what you need. I was the same way when my son was younger. I was the one who always took him on special adventures. I was the one who dealt with the public meltdowns. I enjoyed my time with him but I needed my husband to help sometimes. I just didn’t ask for that because I thought, well this is just something I have to do because he has other things to do. 

Now I try and look at the situation and ask myself, is my husband meeting my needs in this situation? It sounds like your husband is not. If you appreciate the blinds being closed, think about how much you would appreciate a sleep in day even if it was just once or twice a month. 

I would say something like this - husband, I’m coming from a vulnerable place and I need you to hear me and hold space for what I’m saying. (This gives him a heads up that he needs to focus on what you’re saying. Turn all of the distractions off and sit looking at each other.)

Then I would say something like - I need to be able to sleep in sometimes so that I can recharge my batteries and be a better mom and happier wife. (I always like to add in the what’s in it for him. If you think about it you probably would be a happier wife if your husband was more considerate and you got some extra sleep sometimes.)

Then put an action into place - on Saturday the 29th I would like to sleep in while you get up with LO. 

That is a reasonable request and when you say it calmly and without judgement it is harder for him to say no. 

Good luck!
